title: simulate data (health bias) then analysis with cjoint in R
text:
create all possible pairs of statements then choose a random pair


40 simulated participants
6 pairwise comparisons, each gets assigned winner/loser


library(jsonlite)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(cmdstanr)
library(tidybayes)
library(marginaleffects)
library(cjoint)
library(forcats)

df_ci_cjoint<- fromJSON("../../data/conjoint/conjoint_CI_bias.json")
pair_ids = as.data.frame(t(combn(df_ci_cjoint$id,2)))
colnames(pair_ids) <- c("id1","id2")

#all possible comparison pairs
df_pairs <- pair_ids[sample(nrow(pair_ids)), ] 

#empty dataframe for winners/losers from pairwise comparisons
results <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 8, nrow = 0)) 
colnames(results) <- c("c1","c2","c3","c4","c5","c6","response_id","chosen")
results <- results %>%
  mutate(
    c1 = as.character(c1),
    c2 = as.character(c2),
    c3 = as.character(c3),
    c4 = as.character(c4),
    c5 = as.character(c5),
    c6 = as.character(c6),
    response_id = as.integer(response_id),
    chosen = as.numeric(chosen)
  )

# fill survey results dataframe with simulated results
# select random comparison pair to pairwise comparison 
# then choose winner randomly
howmany_participants <- 40 #survey participants
howmany_comparisons <- 6
bias_prob <- 0.8
for (i in 1:howmany_participants) {
  df_survey <- df_pairs[sample(nrow(df_pairs), howmany_comparisons), ]
  #bias goes here
  for (j in 1:howmany_comparisons) {
    if (df_ci_cjoint[df_ci_cjoint$id == df_survey$id1[j],"health"] == TRUE && 
        df_ci_cjoint[df_ci_cjoint$id == df_survey$id2[j],"health"] == FALSE) {
      df_survey[j,"winner"] <- sample(unlist(df_survey[j,1:2]),size=1,prob=c(bias_prob,1-bias_prob),replace=FALSE)
    } else if (df_ci_cjoint[df_ci_cjoint$id == df_survey$id1[j],"health"] == FALSE && 
               df_ci_cjoint[df_ci_cjoint$id == df_survey$id2[j],"health"] == TRUE) {
      df_survey[j,"winner"] <- sample(unlist(df_survey[j,1:2]),size=1,prob=c(1-bias_prob,bias_prob),replace=FALSE)
    } else {
      df_survey[j,"winner"] <- sample(unlist(df_survey[j,1:2]),size=1)
    }
  }
  #  df_survey$winner <- df_survey[cbind(1:nrow(df_survey), sample(1:2, nrow(df_survey), replace = TRUE))]
  df_survey <- df_survey %>%
    mutate(loser = if_else(id1 == winner, id2, id1))
  df_response <- as.data.frame(t(df_survey[,c("winner","loser")])) %>%
    setNames(c("c1","c2","c3","c4","c5","c6")) %>%
    mutate(
      response_id = i,
      chosen = c(1,0)
    )
  results <- bind_rows(results,df_response)
}


create data structure for analysis


# resulting dataframe, with attribute-level info as factor, is analysis data structure
ci_factors_cjoint <- results %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6),
    names_to = "choice number",
    values_to = "id"
  ) %>%
  left_join(df_ci_cjoint, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(across(c(sender,purpose,recipient),as.factor)) %>%
  # refactor with new reference levels: strength coach, load management, head coach
  mutate(sender = fct_relevel(sender, "strength coach")) %>%
  mutate(purpose = fct_relevel(purpose, "load management")) %>%
  mutate(recipient = fct_relevel(recipient, "head coach"))


amce as calculated with cjoint package


# results <- read_csv("qualtrics_export.csv") will need to transform to this data structure
# amce = Average Marginal Component Effects, from cjoint package
# "design" parameter incorporates model constraints

design <- readRDS("../../data/conjoint/cjoint_design.rds")
  
amce_out <- amce(
  chosen ~ sender + purpose + recipient,
  data = ci_factors_cjoint,
  design = design,
  respondent.id = "response_id",
  cluster = TRUE
)
plot(amce_out)

title: simulate data (health bias) then analysis with BradleyTerry2 in R
text:
create all possible pairs of statements then choose a random pair


40 simulated participants
6 pairwise comparisons, each gets assigned winner/loser
bias responses in favor of health-related responses


library(jsonlite)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(cmdstanr)
library(tidybayes)
library(marginaleffects)
library(BradleyTerry2)
library(forcats)

df_ci <- fromJSON("../../data/conjoint/conjoint_CI_bias.json")
pair_ids = as.data.frame(t(combn(df_ci$id,2)))
colnames(pair_ids) <- c("id1","id2")
df_pairs <- pair_ids[sample(nrow(pair_ids)), ] #all possible comparison pairs
results <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 3, nrow = 0)) #dataframe for winners from pairwise comparisons
colnames(results) <- c("id1","id2","outcome")
results <- results %>%
  mutate(
    id1 = as.factor(id1),
    id2 = as.factor(id2),
    outcome = as.integer(outcome)
  )
howmany_participants <- 40 #survey participants
howmany_comparisons <- 6 #comparisons in each survey
bias_prob <- 0.8
for (i in 1:howmany_participants) {
  df_survey <- df_pairs[sample(nrow(df_pairs), howmany_comparisons), ]
  #bias goes here
  for (j in 1:howmany_comparisons) {
    if (df_ci[df_ci$id == df_survey$id1[j],"health"] == TRUE && df_ci[df_ci$id == df_survey$id2[j],"health"] == FALSE) {
      df_survey[j,"outcome"] <- sample(0:1, size=1, prob=c(1-bias_prob,bias_prob), replace=FALSE)
    } else if (df_ci[df_ci$id == df_survey$id1[j],"health"] == FALSE && df_ci[df_ci$id == df_survey$id2[j],"health"] == TRUE) {
      df_survey[j,"outcome"] <- sample(0:1, size=1, prob=c(bias_prob,1-bias_prob), replace=FALSE)
    } else {
      df_survey[j,"outcome"] <- sample(0:1, size=1)
    }
  }
  # df_survey$outcome <- sample(0:1, nrow(df_survey), replace = TRUE)
  results <- bind_rows(results,df_survey) %>%
    mutate(across(c(id1,id2),as.factor)) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.factor), ~ fct_unify(pick(where(is.factor)))[[cur_column()]]))
}


create data structure for analysis


ci <- data.frame(
  Sender = df_ci$sender,
  Purpose = df_ci$purpose,
  Recipient = df_ci$recipient,
  id = df_ci$id,
  row.names = df_ci$id
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Sender,Purpose,Recipient),as.factor))

bt_data <- list(contests = results, predictors = ci)


Bradley Terry model and fixed effects plot


bt_model <- BTm(
  outcome = outcome,
  player1 = id1,
  player2 = id2,
  formula = ~ Sender[id] + Purpose[id] + Recipient[id] + (1 | id),
  id = "id",
  data = bt_data,
  br = TRUE
)

dotchart(
  coef(bt_model),
  main = "Bradley-Terry Fixed Effect Coefficients (random)"
)

ci_factors <- results %>%

    cols = c(c1,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6),

  ) %>%
  left_join(df_ci_cjoint, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(across(c(sender,purpose,recipient),as.factor)) %>%
# need to refactor with new reference levels: s:strength coach, load management, r:head coach
  mutate(sender = fct_relevel(sender, "s:strength coach")) %>%
  mutate(purpose = fct_relevel(purpose, "load management")) %>%
  mutate(recipient = fct_relevel(recipient, "r:head coach"))

# check attributes for uniqueness
check_attr <- c("sender","purpose","recipient")
for (attr in check_attr) {
  raw_levels <- ci_factors[attr]
  if (any(duplicated(unique(raw_levels)))) {
    print(paste("Problem found in attribute: ", attr))
